neighbours.label: noun completing a fixed idiomatic phrase (old hat, back in the days, such a mechanic)
fire: For a veteran sailor like him, storms at sea were old hat by now.
We used to walk to school back in the days before buses.
Missing deadlines seemed to be par for the course at that office.
After the scandal the minister was treated as damaged goods.
Her sudden resignation came as a bolt from the blue.
The new manager tried to keep everyone on the same page.
That cheap repair turned out to be a drop in the bucket.
The old printer finally bit the dust last week.
quiet: For a veteran sailor like him, storms at sea were familiar by now.
We used to walk to school many years before buses.
Missing deadlines seemed to be normal at that office.
After the scandal the minister was treated with suspicion.
Her sudden resignation came as a complete surprise.
The new manager tried to keep everyone informed.
That cheap repair turned out to be far too small.
The old printer finally broke down last week.

notes: Broad pole (1.5%); top examples heterogeneous. Speculative label.
